speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prematurity and rapid onset of symptoms, I suspect Respiratory Distress Syndrome due to surfactant deficiency. Let me examine the infant's chest for signs of grunting, nasal flaring, and intercostal retractions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm infant with early-onset respiratory distress, grunting, and retractions is highly suggestive of Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
